evidence_policy: Real organizations and public URLs, not customers, partners, verified demand, sent outreach or delivered projects.

prospects.mcp_status: A Judge.me Email MCP is documented; a first-party reviews API MCP was not confirmed in this research.
prospects.task: Let merchant agents retrieve source-backed rating summaries and published review evidence for one product.
prospects.offer: API Agent Launch; scoped reviews data access
prospects.hypothesis: A specific reviews intelligence workflow can complement its existing integrations without duplicating its Email MCP.
prospects.subject: Judge.me reviews API → verified product-review tools for AI merchants
prospects.pitch: Your Reviews API and technology partner pathway suggest a practical opportunity: a small, source-backed MCP toolset for merchants to ask for product rating summaries and supporting published reviews in one named AI client. We know Judge.me Email has an MCP connection; this proposal targets review retrieval, not the Email MCP. Could we agree on one approved merchant use case and API scope for a test?

prospects.mcp_status: Public REST API is documented; general first-party customer-data MCP was not verified here. Re-check before pitching.
prospects.task: Let authorized CX analysts retrieve survey status and response aggregates in an agent without exporting raw customer responses.
prospects.hypothesis: CX teams may value a narrow, approved summary layer over exposing entire survey APIs.
prospects.subject: SurveySparrow API: scoped AI assistant access to survey insights
prospects.pitch: Your REST API and partner ecosystem could support a narrow agent-facing use case: an authorized CX user asks for survey status and response summaries without manually exporting data. We would start with an approved read-only source, two agreed acceptance tests and one supported client. Is there a relevant integrations owner to evaluate this with?

prospects.mcp_status: Public store API and app-submission pathway documented; an official Ecwid store-data MCP was not verified here.
prospects.task: Merchant-authorized read-only lookup of catalog and inventory through a customer AI assistant.
prospects.offer: Agency/marketplace pilot, private auth scoped separately
prospects.hypothesis: A focused merchant use case and install guide could be submitted through the existing Ecwid app process.
prospects.subject: Ecwid merchant catalog: focused agent-readiness pilot
prospects.pitch: Ecwid already has a documented store API and app marketplace. We would like to validate a deliberately small merchant-owned AI workflow: product search and current availability, with permissions and tested connection steps. This is not a claim that Ecwid lacks its own AI roadmap; could you point us to the integration-review process for an approved pilot?

prospects.mcp_status: Public API confirmed. Third-party MCP integrations exist; first-party general fulfillment MCP not confirmed.
prospects.task: Allow print-on-demand sellers to check approved catalog variant availability and product metadata in an AI client.
prospects.offer: Scoped Launch or API partner integration
prospects.hypothesis: Catalog research is safer to pilot than fulfillment mutations or billable order placement.
prospects.subject: Printful API: read-only product research in customer AI assistants
prospects.pitch: We are exploring a read-only, merchant-authorized Printful API workflow for product and variant lookup directly from a named AI assistant. Unlike generic API conversion, we would define accepted tasks, source freshness, and install instructions. Would your developer or partner team consider reviewing a narrowly scoped external integration?

prospects.mcp_status: Community MCP proposals/third-party implementations exist; first-party supported core MCP not established from official sources reviewed.
prospects.task: Give publication editors read-only access to published article metadata and topic discovery through an assistant.
prospects.offer: Open-source adapter demo plus integration distribution
prospects.hypothesis: A content-read use case can validate demand before authenticated Admin API work.
prospects.subject: Ghost Content API: reproducible read-only agent workflow proposal
prospects.pitch: I saw the Ghost community discussions around native MCP. We can contribute a narrow, testable Content API use case for assistants—searching and retrieving published posts, with no admin tokens. If useful, we can post a reproducible demonstration and get community feedback before asking for any formal integration listing.

prospects.mcp_status: A Sentry-built community MCP is acknowledged in Plausible docs; a first-party supported MCP is an official roadmap request.
prospects.task: Query website trend summaries with explicit metric definitions, time windows and no raw personal event data.
prospects.offer: Agent tool-evaluation / reliable hosted integration collaboration
prospects.hypothesis: Reliability, metric correctness and documented host setup might complement existing community MCP.
prospects.subject: Plausible Stats API + agent answers: accuracy-focused integration test
prospects.pitch: Plausible already acknowledges the community-built MCP from Sentry and has a dedicated feature request. Rather than suggesting another generic wrapper, we can test a bounded Stats API workflow for accurate period comparisons, explicit metric definitions and reproducible failure handling. Would documented evaluation results help your MCP roadmap?

prospects.mcp_status: Teamleader Orbit has an announced MCP; do not infer that Focus has no AI or MCP capabilities. Focus offers its own API and marketplace.
prospects.task: Authorized small-business staff query sales pipeline and draft quotation status without modifying records.
prospects.hypothesis: A Focus-specific, tested task layer may be valuable despite existing Orbit MCP.
prospects.subject: Teamleader Focus API: targeted AI assistant integration for quote lookups
prospects.pitch: I saw Teamleader Orbit's MCP announcement and Focus's separate developer/Marketplace API. Rather than duplicate Orbit, we would like to discuss a narrowly scoped Focus customer task: read authorized opportunities and quotation status from a named AI client. Is a custom integration submission the right path for a proof-of-value?

prospects.mcp_status: AI features announced; current X-Series documentation did not establish a broadly supported official MCP interface. Verify with partner team.
prospects.task: Retailer inventory lookup by SKU and location using existing customer-granted API scope.
prospects.hypothesis: A merchant-operated agent query may complement native Lightspeed AI, not replace it.
prospects.subject: Lightspeed Retail API: merchant-directed SKU lookup from AI assistants
prospects.pitch: Lightspeed is already investing in native AI, so we are not pitching a generic MCP generator. We are proposing a small retailer-controlled inventory lookup use case for an external assistant, supported by documented API permissions and named-client tests. Would the developer-partner team review this integration category?

prospects.mcp_status: Recharge Analytics MCP Early Adopter Program exists; generic analytics MCP creation is not a viable differentiator.
prospects.task: Merchant support agent reads a subscription's state, billing interval and safe change policies before any modification.
prospects.offer: Technology partner pilot for non-analytics merchant support
prospects.hypothesis: Focus on merchant support permissions and source-scoped read workflows, not a second analytics MCP.
prospects.subject: Recharge API: non-analytics merchant-support MCP use case
prospects.pitch: Recharge already has an Analytics MCP early-adopter offering. Our proposal is different: a permissioned merchant-support read workflow for subscription status and plan policy, with no billing changes or customer action until separately authorized. Is this a relevant gap for your technology-partner team to explore?

prospects.mcp_status: Official Jobber MCP / ChatGPT and Claude connector already launched; do not sell a duplicate general MCP.
prospects.task: Evaluate a specific permitted field-service job-status use case and document AI client acceptance, rather than recreating Jobber MCP.
prospects.offer: Integration QA / vertical workflow, only after validated gap
prospects.hypothesis: Existing native MCP lowers fit; only pursue a verified integration/QA pain.
prospects.subject: Jobber MCP already exists — proposal to validate a specific customer workflow
prospects.pitch: We see that Jobber already ships an official MCP connector. We are not proposing another general connector. If there is a documented gap in a field-service workflow or in external client acceptance, Foundry can run targeted task tests and supply reusable technical evidence. Would your developer team consider a narrow gap assessment?

prospects.mcp_status: Documented REST API and app distribution; a first-party full merchant MCP was not confirmed. Third-party connector listings exist.
prospects.task: Owner-authorized rental inventory lookup and reservation availability by date.
prospects.hypothesis: Rental operators may need availability-aware tools rather than a generic list-all-rentals wrapper.
prospects.subject: Booqable API: dated rental availability from AI assistants
prospects.pitch: I reviewed Booqable's REST API and developer app model. We are testing one specific AI workflow for rental merchants: look up equipment and verify availability for a requested date range with source-backed results, without writing reservations. Would a narrow, owner-authorized read-only demonstration fit your developer app review process? We would document two acceptance tasks and the supported client.

prospects.mcp_status: Official *documentation* MCP exists; it helps developers read API docs. This is not evidence of a merchant operational order-status MCP.
prospects.task: Authorized retailer asks an AI assistant for live shipment state and carrier tracking evidence.
prospects.offer: Scoped shipping API integration / partner test
prospects.hypothesis: Differentiate actual merchant data operations from ShipStation's already-offered Docs MCP.
prospects.subject: ShipStation API: source-backed merchant shipment lookup in AI clients
prospects.pitch: I found your API documentation and the official ShipStation Documentation MCP. We are not proposing another docs helper. Our question is whether merchants need a strictly read-only, authorized assistant workflow to check a shipment's current status and tracking source. We can submit two reproducible tests and host configuration, with no order creation or label purchase. Is the API integration partner program the right evaluation route?

prospects.mcp_status: V5 REST API documented. Independent community MCP implementations/proposals exist; official full-production MCP scope requires rechecking.
prospects.task: A business owner reads overdue invoice status and amounts without initiating payment or changing records.
prospects.hypothesis: Specific accounts-receivable workflows and client acceptance may still need tested, private integration.
prospects.subject: Invoice Ninja v5 API: read-only invoice status for an AI assistant
prospects.pitch: Invoice Ninja already supports API-based automation and community integrations. We would like to validate a narrow customer-owned AI use case: read overdue invoices and status through the v5 API, with per-user authorization, defined accounting fields and no write or payment side effects. Do you have an official MCP roadmap or an integration review contact we should coordinate with before building a reproducible pilot?

prospects.mcp_status: Public developer API and third-party authorization flow documented; an official customer-data MCP was not confirmed by this review.
prospects.task: Authorized booking staff retrieve upcoming sessions and available slots for one specific service.
prospects.hypothesis: Agent answers about availability are concrete user outcomes; third-party permission mechanism must be tested.
prospects.subject: Bookeo API: permissioned booking lookups from AI clients
prospects.pitch: Your API documentation describes an integration and customer authorization path. We are exploring a focused read-only workflow where an authorized booking operator can ask an AI assistant for upcoming reservations and availability without creating or cancelling bookings. Would the API team review a two-task prototype with explicit account scope and installation steps? We would not request access outside Bookeo's approved API process.

prospects.mcp_status: Official v4 developer API documented; native first-party booking operations MCP was not established in research.
prospects.task: Agent reads available tours and reservation status for an authorized account without making a booking.
prospects.hypothesis: High-intent availability/status questions provide narrow acceptance criteria before any write operation.
prospects.subject: Checkfront API: verified booking-status queries in customer AI assistants
prospects.pitch: We reviewed the Checkfront developer API, including its customer authorization model. We propose validating just two read-only tasks in an external AI client: availability for a requested tour/date and status of an authorized booking. The result would include bounded tools, clear credentials handling and source-backed tests. Is there an integration-review contact who could assess this workflow without a broad marketplace commitment?

prospects.mcp_status: REST API and partner ecosystem verified; official general-purpose form-submission MCP status needs verification before outreach.
prospects.task: Authorized operator checks form completion counts and defined workflow status without exposing respondent personal data.
prospects.hypothesis: A minimal sensitive-data approach may improve host compatibility and buyer trust.
prospects.subject: Formstack API: permissioned workflow-status tools for AI assistants
prospects.pitch: Formstack documents a REST API for customer-owned integrations. We are assessing a limited agent workflow for business teams: see active form status and submission counts without exposing raw respondent fields or taking write actions. We would define tenant scope, a compatible host and two source-backed tests before proposing an implementation. Is this best evaluated through developer support or an integration partner channel?

prospects.mcp_status: Developer API and technology integration partner program confirmed; any official MCP and native AI scope should be reconfirmed before approach.
prospects.task: Approved manager retrieves upcoming roster gaps by site and date, without editing employee shifts.
prospects.hypothesis: Manager-only roster questions have concrete benefit but require workforce privacy and partner access scoping.
prospects.subject: Deputy API: manager-authorized roster gap lookup for AI assistants
prospects.pitch: I reviewed your developer API and integration partner program. We are not proposing another general payroll connector. A small pilot could let an authorized manager ask an AI client for unfilled shifts at one location, using the proper Deputy tenant permissions and no shift mutations. Could the partnerships team assess whether this narrow read-only use case is useful and which approved API scopes apply?

prospects.mcp_status: Customer/API-key workflows exist for eligible plans; approved partner and account conditions apply. Native official MCP for customer job lookups was not confirmed.
prospects.task: Eligible customer asks job status and appointment schedule with read-only authorized access.
prospects.hypothesis: Strong field-services task fit, but availability of API access to buyer and partner qualification must be checked first.
prospects.subject: Housecall Pro API: customer-sponsored read-only job lookup
prospects.pitch: Your API guidance describes how eligible customers and developers can build scoped integrations. We would first validate one customer's API access and a read-only job-status task before offering an external AI assistant connector. The pilot would not issue estimates, invoices or job mutations. Is there an integrations contact who could review a customer-sponsored, tightly scoped test?

prospects.mcp_status: JobNimbus Open API documented; first-party official MCP status was not established in this research.
prospects.task: Authorized contractor retrieves project stage and next scheduled service date from CRM.
prospects.hypothesis: A small read-only CRM task offers measurable field acceptance without assuming write privileges.
prospects.subject: JobNimbus API: verified contractor project lookup through AI
prospects.pitch: I reviewed your API authorization and custom integration documentation. We are assessing a bounded, tenant-authorized workflow in which a contractor asks an AI client for one project's stage and upcoming scheduled visit. We would start with read-only permissions, two source-backed task tests and no customer record updates. Is this a suitable use case for an integration review or developer discussion?

prospects.mcp_status: REST-like API documented; official customer-support MCP status and restrictions require updated review.
prospects.task: Customer-support lead reads ticket counts and open conversation metadata without exporting private message bodies.
prospects.hypothesis: Usefulness may come from a bounded support queue summary instead of raw conversation exposure.
prospects.subject: Re:amaze API: support queue summaries in authorized AI clients
prospects.pitch: Your documented REST API provides a path to authorized support workflows. We would like to test a narrow read-only MCP integration for support managers: summarize the open conversation queue and retrieve permitted ticket metadata without leaking customer message content. We would scope one tenant, named AI client and two accepted tasks before commercializing it. Is there a suitable integrations contact to evaluate this proposal?
